summary_hint: County/authority, tax year, property address, and total tax due (with delinquent/lien status) — the annual property-tax figure for the housing payment/DTI, with the land vs improvement assessed split needed to catch new-construction under-assessment.

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity — source/authority that issued the bill

typed_core.name: taxing_authority
typed_core.why: identity — county/municipality/taxing body; DT-4 context

typed_core.name: taxpayer_or_owner_names_raw
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — owners verbatim (flattened from person_or_entity[]); a bad name split stays visible for the tag layer to judge

typed_core.name: taxpayer_or_owner_name
typed_core.why: identity — first assessed owner, matched to borrower / retained-REO owner

typed_core.name: taxpayer_or_owner_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second assessed owner

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: RE-2 — the property this bill documents, matched later to subject vs retained REO
typed_core.prompt_hint: Do NOT decide whether this is the subject property or another owned property — capture the address and parcel so matching happens later

typed_core.name: parcel_or_apn
typed_core.why: identity — parcel key for cross-document matching

typed_core.name: tax_bill_or_account_number
typed_core.why: identity/dedup — bill/account number

typed_core.name: tax_year
typed_core.why: DT-4 / RE-2 — the year the tax figure applies to; recency of the retained-property evidence

typed_core.name: assessment_period
typed_core.why: disambiguator for tax_year — distinguishes fiscal (e.g. 2024-2025) from calendar year

typed_core.name: assessed_land_value
typed_core.why: DT-4 — the new-construction land-only reassessment check reads this; without the split the AI-assist is blind
typed_core.prompt_hint: New construction: the bill may reflect a land-only (unimproved) assessment; capture assessed_land_value and assessed_improvement_value separately so DT-4 can flag that the improved value is not yet assessed and the payment must use the reassessed value

typed_core.name: assessed_improvement_value
typed_core.why: DT-4 — the improved/structure value; the reassessed basis a completed build should be taxed on

typed_core.name: total_assessed_value
typed_core.why: DT-4 — assessed value compared against the tax figure

typed_core.name: taxable_value
typed_core.why: DT-4 disambiguator — tax is computed on taxable (post-exemption) value, not gross assessed
typed_core.prompt_hint: A homestead/owner-occupied exemption reduces taxable value; a new buyer may not inherit the seller's exemption, which changes the estimated tax

typed_core.name: base_tax_amount
typed_core.why: DT-4 — the ad valorem base tax, distinct from special assessments
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish the ad valorem base tax from special assessments (Mello-Roos, CFD, bonds) — both belong on the bill, in different slots

typed_core.name: total_tax_due
typed_core.why: DT-4 — the total tax figure used in the payment/escrow estimate

typed_core.name: current_balance
typed_core.why: RE-2 / processor — amount currently owed on the retained/subject property

typed_core.name: penalties_and_interest
typed_core.why: processor — delinquency charges owed
typed_core.prompt_hint: Penalty + interest (+ costs) currently due — sum of the interest/penalty/costs line items. Capture an explicit 0.00 when those lines are present and zero (bill current). null only if there is no penalty/interest line at all.

typed_core.name: delinquent_or_lien_status
typed_core.why: processor — tax delinquency/lien affects title and escrow setup

typed_core.name: interest_begins_date
typed_core.why: the date interest/penalty begins to accrue on the unpaid bill

typed_core.name: legal_description
typed_core.why: the property legal description (lot/block/subdivision) - distinct from parcel_or_apn

nested_lists.name: installments_and_due_dates
nested_lists.shape_reason: a tax bill carries 1-4 installments (annual / semi-annual / quarterly) — very few items, so a flat row per installment stays far under the 16,384-token ceiling and is simpler than per-field wrapping

fields.name: installment_label
fields.why: DT-4 payment timing — which installment (annual / semi-annual / quarterly)

fields.name: paid_status
fields.why: processor — paid / unpaid state of the installment

fields.name: paid_date
fields.why: processor — when the installment was paid

nested_lists.name: jurisdiction_breakdown
nested_lists.shape_reason: the per-district rate/amount table — a bill splits the total across county / municipality / fire / school districts, each with its own rate. Captured for future tax-composition rules; no live consumer yet (LP-460).

fields.name: amount_billed
fields.why: the amount billed for the district

fields.name: adjusted_billed
fields.why: the adjusted billed amount, if shown

rejected.name: subject_property_indicator
rejected.reason: a judgment the extractor cannot read faithfully — a tax bill never declares itself the 'subject'; matching/RE-2 decides it. Contradicts the prompt's own 'do not decide which property' instruction

rejected.name: party_names / party_addresses
rejected.reason: duplicate taxpayer_or_owner_names — on a tax bill the parties are the assessed owners

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: a tax bill is not a standardized form; catch-all

rejected.name: statement_period_start / _end
rejected.reason: a tax bill is not a periodic statement

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a tax bill is not an executed/notarized instrument

rejected.name: legal_description
rejected.reason: long text, no rule/processor need; catch-all

rejected.name: loan_number
rejected.reason: not present on a taxing-authority bill

rejected.name: exemptions_or_credits, tax_rates_or_millage, special_assessments_or_charges, payments_and_paid_dates
rejected.reason: object[] beyond the one nested-list budget -> additional_sections (exemptions & special assessments flagged in Open questions)

encoding_variations: Assessed vs taxable vs 'full cash value' vs 'net taxable' — issuers label the tax base differently; DT-4 must compare against the base the tax is actually computed on (taxable_value), not gross total_assessed_value.
Tax year vs fiscal year — CA bills state '2024-2025'; others state a calendar year. assessment_period is the disambiguator.
Total tax may include or exclude special assessments (Mello-Roos / CFD / bond) — ad valorem base vs grand total. base_tax_amount vs total_tax_due carry both.

options: keep as a typed bool per the catalog
reject as a conclusion the extractor cannot read from the bill
open_questions.recommendation: (b) — a tax bill has no field stating it is the subject; RE-2 and downstream matching own that call, and the existing prompt explicitly says not to decide. Confirm before shipping

open_questions.q: Homestead/exemptions as a DT-4 disambiguator. Loss of a seller's homestead exemption on a new purchase raises the effective tax, which is exactly DT-4's under-estimate concern.
options: promote a flattened exemptions_summary / homestead_exemption_present typed field
open_questions.recommendation: revisit (b) with the domain expert — currently left to catch-all to respect the one-list budget GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Special assessments and DT-4. Should the escrow/payment estimate include Mello-Roos/CFD special assessments, or only the ad valorem base? This determines whether DT-4 should read total_tax_due or base_tax_amount.
open_questions.recommendation: carry both (done) and let the rule authors choose; flag for domain-expert confirmation

open_questions.q: installments list shape — 1-4 items is firmly within budget for flat rows; no per-field wrap needed.

notes: 19 typed-core fields — appropriate for a Tier-2 document whose 2 rules concentrate on the assessed values and the tax figure; the remainder are identity/disambiguators a processor needs to attach the bill to the right property.

property_address and taxpayer_or_owner_name(s) are typed so they are not stored raw in the catch-all; recommend NOT masking (public tax record + RE-2/DT-4 match keys would break) — not in the 7-field _PII_FIELDS registry, pre_masked=false if registered. No SSN/DOB/full-account number appears on a property-tax bill.
Ambiguity: taxing_authority classed identity with DT-4 in rules ('DT-4 context'); current_balance classed rule (leads 'RE-2 / processor') — both have a defensible processor reading.
